However, the evidence also shows a compounded sales growth of only 18% over the last three years [E15] and trailing twelve-month sales growth of just 25% [E17]. This slower growth in revenue suggests that any recent performance might be more cyclical than structural. In conclusion, while SHILPAMED has shown some positive momentum recently, its long-term performance and current valuation metrics do not support the bull's argument.
